notes: Covers the DC25 range as Dyson's service manual (marked Issued Feb 08) describes it: a motor and yoke assembly plus a separate brushbar motor with its own belt in the cleaner head. The manual names parts and where they sit but gives no part numbers or ratings.

gaps: The 96 C thermal cut-out and the 60-minute shutdown are only in ManualsLib's question-and-answer text, not in the manual's own pages; the thermal cut-out part and the TCO reset mention were left out.
No volts, watts, amps, cord length or part numbers appear in the pages read, and neither motor's type is given.
The brushbar motor is filed under motor_universal as a catalogue bucket only; no source gives its type.
The manual says it covers the full DC25 range and does not separate variants; it is marked 'Issued Feb 08', the manual's date, not a production range.
ManualsLib viewer page 1 shows only excerpts of the manual; pages not shown there were not read.
The electrical circuit page (viewer page 6) has a resistance table that the text extraction scrambles, so no resistance values are recorded.
method: Dyson DC25 Service Manual on ManualsLib (manual 2911654): titled 'Dyson DC25 Service Manual', Issued Feb 08, written for Dyson trained engineers, covers the full DC25 range. Read with the fetch tool.
Viewer page 1 shows excerpts of manual pages 7, 11-12, 28-50, 53, 57 and 64-65 plus FAQ text; page 2 is the contents list; page 21 is the motor and yoke fitting.
Page numbers in the specs are ManualsLib viewer pages, which match the manual's contents list.

A plain command-line request to ManualsLib got a Cloudflare challenge and was not pursued; the fetch tool's reads of the three pages showed no challenge, login or paywall, and repeated reads gave the same quotes.

comps.spec: Motor and yoke assembly; its fitting steps involve a motor bucket with its wiring assembly, a motor mount and an inlet bucket seal (viewer page 21)

Brushbar motor with its own motor cover in the cleaner head; it is off when the machine stands upright, runs when the machine is tilted into normal vacuuming mode, and can be switched off with the brushbar switch (pp. 7, 64)
Brushbar drive belt, fitted over the motor pulley and the drive wheel; reaching it means removing the soleplate screws, the endcap and the brushbar assembly (pp. 64-65)
Upright switch, operated when the machine tilts into normal vacuuming mode, and a brushbar switch; the switch is attached to the live wires from the powercord and internal cable (pp. 7, 47)
Powercord assembly, fed through a cable protector fitted into the side of the duct assembly (pp. 45-47)

Valve hose assembly that connects at the side of the duct assembly, and a separate wand assembly; the manual has sections on valve hose replacement and on hose and wand sub-assemblies (pp. 37, 43, contents)
